headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs for new grid infrastructure necessitated by their demand, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger's office, consumer advocates, environmental advocates, Appalachian Voices, State Corporation Commission (SCC) staff.
opponents: Hyperscalers (Meta, Google, Amazon, Microsoft) initially opposed mandatory direct cost allocation.
news_headline: Virginia requires firms to pay for dedicated electrical infrastructure
news_summary: Virginia has mandated that data centers pay for their own dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure following significant electricity price hikes, largely attributed to the massive power demand of these facilities. Governor Spanberger's office and state regulators assert this measure will save residential ratepayers hundreds of millions of dollars and prevent further price increases.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill establishes requirements for data centers to report their water consumption, aiming to increase transparency and inform sustainable water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental advocates (Sierra Club), state regulators (DEQ), Governor's office.
opponents: Data Center Industry (implied, due to potential for increased regulation).
news_headline: Virginia study on groundwater, data centers calls for tighter water regulations
news_summary: A recent Virginia state report highlights that the groundwater supply in the eastern coastal plain is constrained and recommends stronger regulatory authority for rejecting industrial water withdrawal permits, especially for water-intensive facilities like data centers. The study suggests that most new large industrial groundwater withdrawals are unlikely to be sustainable under current conditions.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill empowers local governments to establish and enforce specific regulations regarding the siting of data centers and limits on the noise they produce.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community advocacy groups, environmental groups, local supervisors.
opponents: Data center industry (e.g., Compass Datacenters, Vantage Data Centers).
news_headline: Loudoun County homeowners are fed up with data center noise
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are increasingly vocal about constant industrial hums and diesel fumes from nearby data centers, which they report are impacting their quality of life, sleep, and health. Local officials are facing pressure to re-evaluate noise ordinances and enforce stricter regulations on data center operations, especially concerning backup generators.
